justification: The system demonstrates high statistical parity across demographic groups A and B. Specifically, the false-positive rates (8.1% vs 8.7%), false-negative rates (6.4% vs 6.8%), and calibration errors (0.031 vs 0.034) are closely aligned. Additionally, the evaluation was performed on a large, representative validation dataset and independently reproduced.
evidence_used: False-positive rate for demographic group A: 8.1%
False-positive rate for demographic group B: 8.7%
False-negative rate for demographic group A: 6.4%
False-negative rate for demographic group B: 6.8%
Calibration error: 0.031 for demographic group A and 0.034 for demographic group B
The documented demographic composition of the validation dataset is within 2.5 percentage points of the estimated composition of the intended deployment population for groups A and B
The subgroup calculations were reproduced by a validation team that did not develop the model
limitations: The assessment is limited to mathematical and statistical definitions of fairness (predictive parity and error rate balance) and does not account for other qualitative, historical, or systemic dimensions of fairness.
